steps.text: Stir the cranberry juice cocktail, water, brown sugar, cinnamon stick, and allspice together in a saucepan; bring to a boil. Add the cherries to the cranberry juice mixture; cook another 2 minutes. Add the cranberries; continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the cranberries pop, about 10 minutes. Remove from heat and chill in refrigerator 8 hours to overnight. Remove and discard cinnamon stick before serving.

review.reviewBody: This is really a lovely recipe! The subtle layering of flavors and the perfect contrast between sweet and tart were heavenly. This will be replacing my nice, but boring old standard recipe. I followed to the letter however, must admit to using a black cherry/cranberry juice blend I found. My only, albeit slight, issue with this recipe is it was a tad 'loose' so I would reduce the juice accordingly next time to allow the sauce to gel a bit thicker. Thank you so much for sharing this gem!

1128.20 ... https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/219607/dried-cherry-and-cranberry-sauce/ ... 'First time making cranberry sauce. Dried cherries are very good in it! I omitted the water, reduced sugar to 3/4c & thickened with 1T cornstarch. Pretty yummy! :)

Wonderful. Because I like the flavor of orange zest I *was* going to zest some orange peel into it. Not finding my zester, I said "What the heck?" and quartered an orange and threw it in the pot with the rest of the ingredients. I let the sauce cook down before removing from the heat; and I left the orange quarters but removed before serving. I buy ground korintje cinnamon in bulk, so I used that rather than a cinnamon stick. Absolutely delicious (and let me throw in a plug for buying cinnamon other than what one picks up in the grocery store. you will not believe the difference in the flavor!)

11.21.19 I used Ocean Spray® 5 Calorie Cranberry Drink (what was in the fridge) instead of their cranberry juice cocktail and cut the sugar back to 3/4 cup (personal taste preference). The combination of dried cherries, fresh cranberries, and cranberry drink really works, and for us, this had the perfect balance of sweet-tart. Simply put, it’s full-bodied, vibrant, and not excessively sweet. I’ve made a lot of cranberry sauce recipes on this site, and this one ranks right up there at the top.

This was the first time I made homemade cranberry sauce ever, and it was so easy and delicious. I made it for Thanksgiving dinner and everyone really loved it. Even my husband, who only eats the canned jelly sauce, liked it, and my mother, who can be very difficult to please, requested that I bring it to Christmas dinner. This is definitely going to be a regular offering at holiday dinners! The only difference I made was that I added maybe two more ounces of tart Montgomery cherries (total 8ozs instead of 6ozs) because the bag came in 8ozs and it was just easier to use the whole thing, but I compensated by adding slightly more cranberries. Was amazing in the end!

I made this tonight and wow, is it ever delicious! The two fruits are really great combined, and the cinnamon and allspice are perfect. Nothing overwhelms other flavors. I can't do sugar being diabetic, so used "diet" cranberry juice and substituted agave syrup for the brown sugar (not sure how much, just a really good squeeze). I prefer things to be more tart than sweet, so this was perfect. I also didn't measure exactly 6 oz. of cherries, but sort of estimated since I had no scale and just went by the approximate weight of what I bought in bulk today. I ate some, too, so who knows if exactly 6 ounces wound up in there, LOL! It came out wonderfully, and my roommate, who doesn't even like cranberry, said it smelled so good that she had to try it...and she loved it! It was a little juicy, but thickened up nicely as it cooled.
I love this recipe, I made one change. Instead of cranberry juice cocktail, I use cranberry cherry juice cocktail. Wonderful!

Best cranberry sauce I have made...and I have tried many from this site. I tried making this with both all-natural, no sugar added dried cherries...and then the regular sugar sweetened ones. The sugar sweetened ones in it were much better...just too tart otherwise.
A family member made this over Thanksgiving and I fell in love with the recipe! I just made some and it turned out perfectly. So easy and so delicious!!
Delicious as is. I didn't make any changes. I used it on chicken and yogurt alike!
Such a great tasting sauce and so easy to make. I use this all year long, not just on holidays. Great on yogurt for breakfast too.
This was wonderful. Didn't change a thing. Will absolutely make this every year for Thanksgiving.

WAY to cinnamony? cinnamie? yeah way to much cinnamon in the end result.

other than that it was okay.
Best cranberry sauce ever! It's not as tart as the traditional.

Very good and easy recipe. Followed as written. To me, the allspice gave this an interesting flavor. Tasted like something my European grandmother from Germany would have made. It is not watery, but not thickened either, next time I might try adding some cornstarch to thicken just a bit. It would be good without the addition of allspice too, but the allspice does give it a holiday feel. Gave it 4 stars because it is not my favorite cranberry sauce, but this is very good.

I made this recipe several years back and now it is a family favorite on my Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's table. I'll never use another recipe for Cranberries.
I wish I could can it.
I served it at Thanksgiving. My sister said it's the best cranberry sauce she's ever had. No leftovers of this.
